decisions.statement: This hook judges nothing and refuses no call.
A call is handed back with the line reading the weighing script above it.
The command an agent wrote is left whole below that line.
This hook is named to sort after every hook that judges a bash call.
Each of those judges the command the agent wrote rather than the wrapped one.
The script is reached through the index rather than by a path spelled here.
What a call spent is appended beside the page of the seat the call was made from.
A call a subagent made is weighed against that subagent's seat.
Which file the line goes in is settled here, so a line rolls at the ceiling.
The fill is judged by the whole line rather than by the line's opening.
The rest of that line is written by the shell and counted at its widest.
A call is named by the first line the agent wrote rather than by the whole command.
A word handed to the shell is quoted so the shell reads that word whole.
The groups calls left behind are taken away as the next call opens.
A group named for a process still running is left where it is.
A call this could not weigh is handed back unchanged rather than refused.
A seat whose page is not there is a call handed back unchanged.
A throw anywhere here is a call handed back unchanged.
Nothing here reads what the call answered.

definition: the hook putting a bash call in a group of its own so what that call spends is known
